title: ticfac Phase 6: Cloudflare Computer executor
description: SPEC §12 Phase 5 and §8.3-8.7. Computer executor without changing Job* or role contracts; pin the preview dependency; test Workspace persistence, explicit backend routing, cancellation, inspection/adoption, collection, disposal; phase-aware isolate-to-container promotion, container kept hot through RGR/TDD; shadow the Sandbox executor before changing defaults. Re-read §8.3-8.5 against the API that actually ships before implementing.
notes:
2026-09-17 - MOVED from the ticks tracker to ticfac's own. The ticfac phase ladder was being tracked in ticks under task hzm, which is why ticfac's roadmap showed no Cloudflare work at all. The phases now sit as top-level epics here, alongside qeu (Phase 1), av8 (Phase 2) and 9pd (Phase 3). Nothing in the family referenced anything outside it and no id collided, so the move is the files plus two re-pointings: the parent hzm is dropped, and ncv's blocker becomes 9pd.
2026-09-19 19:37 - 2026-09-19 — renumbered Phase 5 -> Phase 6 and blocked on dha. Phase 4 (ncv) built the Cloudflare host's components but no run driven by them; dha now does that as Phase 5. This epic's gate repeats a Phase 4 gate run that never happened, so it cannot start until dha performs one. From ncv close-out finding 298640ea.
2026-09-22 15:24 - GATED ON xte, WHICH BUILDS THE THING THIS EPIC SHADOWS AGAINST (2026-09-22).

This epic's own plan says 'shadow the Sandbox executor before changing defaults'. Until
today there was no Sandbox executor to shadow: internal/exec/ implements herdr and
subprocess only, and runstate.Executors reserves the name 'cloudflare-sandbox' with
nothing behind it. xte is that implementation, so yvi now blocks on it.

They are successive, not duplicate. xte gets one Sandbox per tick running pi on GLM 5.3
and is the minimum that lets a cloud epic run at all. yvi is the richer API on top -
Workspace persistence, explicit backend routing, phase-aware isolate-to-container
promotion - and the operator's read is that Computer is a superset of Sandbox that can
instantiate a plain isolate for lighter work. That superset relationship is what makes
shadowing the right migration and what makes the order matter.

The instruction to 're-read the spec against the API that actually ships' stands and is
now more pointed: xte will have established what the Sandbox binding really does from a
container, which is evidence this epic should start from rather than re-derive.
acceptance_criteria: Gate: the Phase 4 gate run repeated on the Computer executor, shadowed against Sandbox, with matching evidence.
